clue.text: Trouble afoot at college for these legendary beasts

parts.note: uni is the everyday short form of university, a college in the broad sense
corns are painful patches of hard skin, literally trouble on the feet

explanation.surface: A student's sore feet at college are blamed on mythical creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the pieces in reverse order; the charade still reads college first, then the foot trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Unicorns are horned horses of myth and legend, the classic fabulous beast.

clue.text: Errant Becks run in, admitting two wives separately here in Canada

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one letter is let into the scrambled letters
separately says the two letters go in at different places rather than together
errant means straying or wandering, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife, taken twice here
W is the standard abbreviation for wife, taken twice here

explanation.surface: David Beckham, playing badly, scores and shows off two wives on a trip to Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Errant' scrambles BECKS RUN IN; 'admitting' and 'separately' put a W into it at two different places.
explanation.definitionFit: New Brunswick is one of Canada's Atlantic provinces, so the phrase points to a place within that country.

clue.text: How the convict broke free in emporium?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a prisoner escaped when the ... was ripped apart
an emporium is a large shop, like one branch of a retail group

explanation.surface: A riddle asking how a prisoner escaped inside a big shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer differently and it describes the prisoner tearing his shackles.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large retail shop, and a branch of a multiple retailer is exactly that kind of outlet.

clue.text: Flower lady alone around noon — a typical sight in church

parts.note: the rose is a familiar flower

indicators.note: around means the word for the bereaved lady surrounds the single letter

parts.note: a widow is a woman left alone after her husband's death

explanation.surface: A lonely woman holding flowers at midday is a familiar figure in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose window is a circular stained-glass window with radiating tracery, common in Gothic churches.

clue.text: Sniffer's initial carp?

indicators.note: initial picks out just the opening letter of the nose-owner's word

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Someone with a nose makes their first complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' looks like a verb, to complain, but here it is a fish; read whole, the clue is what a sniffer would first grumble about.
explanation.definitionFit: A foul smell is the first thing a nose would complain of, so the whole clue describes a bad odour.

clue.text: Cut through one denomination headed by bishop

indicators.note: headed by puts the cleric's letter at the front of the rest

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
I is the Roman numeral for one
a sect is a religious group or denomination

explanation.surface: A religious body is split by schism, with a bishop at its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to divide into two parts, which means cutting right across something.

clue.text: Heat up meaty drink shunned by Queen Victoria

indicators.note: shunned by means the queen's initials are left out of the drink's name

parts.note: Bovril is a British beef-extract paste made into a hot savoury drink
VR stands for Victoria Regina, Queen Victoria

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria refuses to warm up a beef drink.
explanation.walkthrough: BOVRIL is a British beef-extract drink; VR is Victoria Regina, so removing it leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To boil something is to heat it until it bubbles, an intense form of heating.

clue.text: Most dumpy workers in group avoiding last time trial

indicators.note: avoiding last says the final letter of the work gang's word is dropped

parts.note: a squad is a group of people working together
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A cycling time trial in which the stockiest team members drop out last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time trial' looks like one cycling term but gives two pieces: T and TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Squat means short and thickset, so the superlative describes whoever is stubbiest of all.

clue.text: President reformed prisoner after tea

indicators.note: after says the shuffled inmate comes behind the drink

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: reformed means the letters of the inmate's word are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A former convict, now going straight, takes over the presidency after a tea break.
explanation.definitionFit: The president of a meeting or society is the person who presides, the one in the chair.

clue.text: Subtly alters complex task, hampering the two of us

indicators.note: hampering means getting in the way, so the pronoun sits in the middle of the jumbled letters
complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters of the job are tangled

parts.note: we means the speaker plus one other

explanation.surface: Someone fine-tunes a complicated job that is getting in the way of a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a small adjustment, so making tweaks means changing something slightly.

clue.text: Painkiller disreputable characters produced, best avoided possibly

indicators.note: avoided says the letters of the second word are taken away from the pool
possibly signals the remaining letters can be arranged into something new

explanation.surface: Shady types produced a painkilling drug that is best steered clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of DISREPUTABLE, remove those of BEST, and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidural is an anaesthetic injected near the spine, often given in childbirth to block pain.

clue.text: See 2
What's essential for new business venture north of Rome, say

indicators.note: north of puts the gamble first, above the city word in a down answer

parts.note: to risk something is to venture it
Rome is an example of a capital city

explanation.surface: A daring enterprise in northern Italy needs something essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Start-ups depend on investment money put up at a hazard, often called venture funding.

clue.text: See 3
Expert's line of reasoning a substitute for the real thing

definitions.text: a substitute for the real thing

parts.note: a pro is an expert, with the 's adding S
a thesis is an argued proposition or line of reasoning

explanation.surface: A specialist's argument is a stand-in for the genuine article.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosthesis is an artificial body part, such as a false leg, standing in for the natural one.

clue.text: Inscrutable question master?

parts.note: the legendary creature at Thebes posed riddles and gave nothing away, a quizmaster who is impossible to read

explanation.surface: A poker-faced host of a quiz show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek monster of Thebes set travellers a riddle, and its name is used for anyone enigmatic.

clue.text: Herald dashing to catch British engineers heading north

indicators.note: to catch means the running word closes round the single letter

parts.note: haring means running fast like a hare

indicators.note: heading north in a down answer means the letters are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A messenger runs to intercept British army engineers travelling north.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, read upwards gives ER at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbinger is a forerunner announcing that something is coming, as a herald does.

clue.text: Cockney trios said to form fancy band

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, says th as f, so threes come out as frees

explanation.surface: Groups of three East End Londoners form a fashionable musical band.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech turns the th sound into f, so threes become frees, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a decorated horizontal strip along a wall, an ornamental band.

clue.text: Grant admission for old boy returning big bottle

indicators.note: admission for means the film star's first name lets the other piece in

parts.note: Cary Grant was a Hollywood film star

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation is turned back to front

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil coming back is let in after being awarded a grant.
explanation.definitionFit: A carboy is a large glass or plastic bottle, often encased, used for chemicals or wine.

clue.text: I carried in sparkling wines in this case

indicators.note: carried in means the single letter is held within the wines

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine, here in the plural

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of carrying fizzy wines in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a box for the bottles but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the present state of affairs, the way things stand, much like 'in this situation'.

clue.text: Struck, as rock is often

definitions.meaning: coins are struck, stamped out by a press at the mint
seaside rock, a British hard candy stick, is usually peppermint flavoured

explanation.surface: A stone being hit, as often happens.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock is the British seaside sweet: a hard sugar stick, typically peppermint.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins are stamped at a mint, and peppermint-flavoured sweets are described as flavoured with mint.

clue.text: Intricate source of visual reception?

parts.note: the complex bundle of fibres carrying signals from the eye to the brain, read as if it were a TV aerial

explanation.surface: A complicated aerial or satellite dish feeding a television picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The nerve from the eye relays visual signals to the brain, so it is where sight is received.

clue.text: Delicate musical variation that's no good for male conductor

parts.note: light means delicate, as in a light touch

indicators.note: for means one abbreviation stands in place of another

parts.note: Nimrod is the best-known of Elgar's Enigma Variations

explanation.surface: A gentle piece of music fails to suit a man wielding the baton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' looks like an orchestra leader, but it is a conductor of electricity; NIMROD is Elgar's famous variation.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal spike on a building carries strikes from storms safely to earth, conducting the current.

clue.text: See 21
Indian ascetic elected after agreement in Berlin

parts.note: ja is German for yes
in means elected, as a candidate who gets in

explanation.surface: An Indian holy man wins a vote after a deal is struck in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the elected piece comes after, matching the order in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jainism is an ancient Indian religion whose monks practise strict self-denial and non-violence.

clue.text: Unwholesome bread found by dog in street

indicators.note: in places the two pieces within the abbreviation for street
found by means the bread is placed right beside the following word

parts.note: to tag is to follow closely, to dog
naan is an Indian flatbread, also spelt nan

explanation.surface: Stale bread discovered by a dog lying in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is still and foul, so the word describes something stale and unhealthy.

clue.text: A writer regularly dividing extremists in Sorbonne?

definitions.text: A writer regularly dividing extremists in Sorbonne?

indicators.note: dividing means those picked letters split the end letters apart
extremists in points to the outermost letters of the university's name
regularly takes every other letter of the opening two words

explanation.surface: A writer at the Paris university who regularly split radicals.
explanation.definitionFit: The French existentialist philosopher and novelist studied in Paris and was a famously divisive radical figure.

clue.text: See 22
Two thirds of tosses involving gold coin

indicators.note: involving means the shortened word wraps round the metal
two thirds of means only four of the six letters of the throws are kept

parts.note: flings are tosses or throws
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Two out of three coin tosses come up gold.
explanation.walkthrough: A florin was an old British coin worth two shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: The florin was a coin, first Florentine gold, later a British two-shilling piece.

clue.text: What happens on New Year's Eve, assuming sun goes down

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the extra letter is taken inside

parts.words: What happens on New Year's Eve
parts.note: on that night December ends, Dec ends

explanation.surface: On the last night of the year the sun sets.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as DEC ENDS, December finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To descend is to move downward, sink or drop, as the sun does at dusk.
